quickAnswerHtml: Bunloet (Pom Prap Sattru Phai) is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in the Nang Loeng area, with a budget of around THB 40-95 per dish. No booking — it's walk-in queue only

blocks.html:
If you had to pick one bowl of egg noodles worth the trip out to Nang Loeng, we'd say "Bunloet" first. This place is a legend at the mouth of Nakhon Sawan 8 alley, in the Nang Loeng market–Wat Sommanat area, open since 1976, named after its founder, with the craft passed down from father to son right up to today. That kind of staying power isn't luck — the MICHELIN guide has awarded it a Bib Gourmand every year running from 2021 through 2026, six years straight for a shophouse noodle stall selling dishes under 100 baht. That's proof the food is genuinely solid, not a fleeting trend.

The heart of the place is the charcoal-grilled soy-sauce pork — pork shoulder marinated in soy sauce, sugar, and pepper, then grilled over charcoal in batches. That smoky char is exactly what turns the egg-noodle-with-grilled-pork bowl into the restaurant's signature dish. Thin, springy egg noodles topped with fragrant grilled pork, just 60-80 baht a bowl. If noodles aren't your thing, there's also red pork and crispy pork over rice, and don't skip the stewed chicken wings at 80 baht a plate — another standout here. Overall prices run 40-95 baht a dish, so eating your fill costs under 100 baht per head. In an era when plenty of MICHELIN noodle spots keep nudging prices up, this one still holds a genuine street-food price point. There's seating for about 40, plus an air-conditioned section to escape the heat — that only costs an extra 5 baht per head, which is a nice touch.

One thing worth knowing before you go: the hours have changed from the old days. Bunloet used to be a late-night spot well known to the graveyard-shift crowd, but now it's open daily during the day, roughly 09:00/10:00 to about 17:00 (some 2025 reviews mention closing around 6pm), and once they sell out, that's it for the day — especially the charcoal-grilled pork, which is grilled in batches. Go too late and you risk missing the best thing on the menu. So if you see old information online saying it's open late at night, don't trust it — plan a daytime visit instead so you don't miss out on anything. Sitting down to a bowl of charcoal-grilled noodles in an old neighbourhood like Nang Loeng, still surrounded by the market and old-style shophouses, gives you a genuine slice of Bangkok you just can't find in a mall.

blocks.descHtml:
Easy on the wallet — 40-95 baht a dish, egg-noodle-with-grilled-pork bowls at 60-80 baht, stewed chicken wings at 80 baht, eating your fill costs under 100 baht per head. The restaurant is walk-in only with no booking system, though you can call ahead to ask or pre-order at 06-2624-9269. Seating is about 40 spots, with an air-conditioned section (an extra 5 baht per head), cash only, and delivery available through the apps if you'd rather not make the trip.

Timing your visit is the most important part. The restaurant is open daily during the day, roughly 09:00/10:00-17:00, and once they sell out, that's it — go before 3pm if you can, especially if you're set on the charcoal-grilled soy-sauce pork, which is cooked in batches and, once gone, means waiting or missing out. As for getting there, the restaurant is at 360, at the mouth of Nakhon Sawan 8 alley, Nakhon Sawan Road, Pom Prap Sattru Phai district, in the Nang Loeng market–Wat Sommanat area — there's no train station within walking distance, so the closest option is connecting from MRT Sam Yot or Hua Lamphong; a taxi or motorbike taxi the rest of the way is the easier bet.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead?
faq.a: No, and you can't — it's walk-in only. You can call ahead to ask or pre-order at 06-2624-9269. Seating is about 40 spots, with an air-conditioned section for an extra 5 baht per head, cash only
Under 100 baht per person. Dishes run 40-95 baht, egg-noodle-with-grilled-pork is 60-80 baht, and stewed chicken wings are 80 baht — one of the lightest budgets among Bib Gourmand picks
Egg-noodle-with-grilled-pork is the signature dish — soy-sauce-marinated pork shoulder grilled over charcoal, very fragrant — followed by red pork and crispy pork over rice, and stewed chicken wings

faq.q: How do I get there, and what time should I go?
faq.a: The restaurant is at the mouth of Nakhon Sawan 8 alley in the Nang Loeng area, with no train station within walking distance — you'll need to connect from MRT Sam Yot or Hua Lamphong. Open daily during the day, roughly 09:00/10:00-17:00. Go before 3pm since the grilled pork sells out in batches
